notes: Checked county economic development/EDA pages and local search. Amelia promotes Amelia County Industrial Park and Regional Commerce Park with M-1 land, broadband, water/sewer, and an April 2026 EDA packet lists 'data center development' as a regional target sector, but I found no named data center developer, permit, rezoning, purchase agreement, or project announcement in Amelia County.

Checked Amherst County planning/document pages and local news. County posted a Planning Commission data center workshop and WSET reported draft restrictions after residents worried a data center might come to a cleared Kings Road site in Madison Heights, but the reporting describes concern and ordinance work rather than a filed/announced project, developer, permit, or approval.

status_detail: AVAIO signed an agreement with the Appomattox County EDA to buy the Appomattox Center for Business and Commerce site; county EDA page hosts approved site plan/SWM documents. AVAIO describes the 436-acre campus at 267 Industrial Park Ln as construction-ready with site plan approved, 300 MW total grid power and up to 700 MW behind-the-meter baseload, with initial 50 MW grid power expected in Q3 2027.
notes: Official county press release says 452-acre site and 300 MW confirmed from CVEC/Dominion; AVAIO current project page gives 436 acres and 1,000 MW total baseload power, so capacity_mw records AVAIO's current total-power figure.

Checked Arlington County site search, Arlington local news, and data-center searches. Results were county IT/data-center consolidation, employment-board listings, or broader Northern Virginia references; I found no county-level commercial/hyperscale data center project in Arlington County. ARLnow noted Arlington has mostly stayed out of the data center game due to limited land.

Checked county/EDA pages and local reporting. Augusta County Economic Development has a 'Regional Data Center' link, but that is demographic/workforce data, not a facility. Local reporting and Shenandoah Alliance quote county officials saying data centers were by-right in General Industrial districts and the county was drafting a dedicated ordinance, while also noting nobody had talked about building one there yet.

Checked Bath County data center/server farm searches and official-site targeted searches. Results were unrelated services pages, Bath County Pumped Storage references, demographic/state data-center references, or solar listings; no named data center facility, developer, permit, rezoning, or local announcement was found for Bath County.

Checked Bedford County business/economic development, news, and town/county searches. Official county business pages list EDA-owned business parks and development resources, while search results only surfaced government technology recognition and discussion about planning ahead should data-center proposals arise; no specific data center project, developer, permit, or approval was found in Bedford County.

Checked Bland County official site, industrial sites/EDA pages, county news, and targeted data-center searches. The county promotes I-77/I-81 access and New River Valley Commerce Park links, but I found no named data center project, developer, permit, rezoning, or approval. Search hits about Hitachi Energy mention supplying data center/infrastructure sectors, not a Bland County data center.

project_name: Google Data Center Campus at Greenfield
aliases: Google Botetourt County Data Center Campus
status_detail: Botetourt County says the project was publicly announced June 24, 2025 after EDA approval of a performance agreement on June 20 and Board support on June 24; the Board/Planning Commission had approved a November 26, 2024 zoning amendment permitting data centers in the RAM district at Botetourt Center at Greenfield. Google confirmed in March 2026 it was moving forward, with mass grading in coming months, while federal/state environmental permits remained under review. County page says Google bought a 312-acre parcel; local records reporting describes three data center buildings totaling nearly 1 million square feet.
notes: No reliable MW capacity found in official county materials; 79.3 MW Rocky Forge Wind PPA is an energy procurement figure, not the campus IT/electrical capacity.

Checked Bristol Virginia official zoning and targeted local searches. The zoning ordinance permits 'Data center or call center' in at least one district, but I found no Bristol, VA-specific data center project, developer, permit, rezoning, or approval. Several 'Bristol data center' results were Bristol, Connecticut or Bristol, Tennessee moratorium items and were excluded.
